- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.5) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots downward in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast dip by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative mid-period, model frequently underreacts — increase forecast sensitivity to sentiment shift by 1–2 steps ahead.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 1–2% upward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
